items.title: 52031_Kenny Clarke oral history interview
items.q: So we went to Boston with Ella... So she stayed back in the restaurant with me... So that was one time Ella was on my side

ctx.x: Then I came back to Minton's and finished the winter out there. And then Diz and I -- this was in 1942, now. This was in '40 also, because Diz was married in -- no, '41, that's right. So we went to Boston with Ella. It was Eddie Bearfield.
Yeah, just shortly after Chick died.

items.title: 52031_Kenny Clarke oral history interview
items.q: call her Sis, you know. I said, 'Sis, I'm not going on until that cat gives me my check.'

ctx.x: So he says, "Well, we have to take it out." So I said, "Well, I'm not going on." So Ella says, "Well, if Kenny's not going on, I'm not going on either." So they had kind of a billiard room in the back, so we were starting to play billiards, and I said, "I'm not going on until you give me my check." So the manager of the Cocoanut Grove, he was saying, "Well, listen now, you must go on." And she said, "Well, we're having a little difficulty. Now, I'll let you know." He says, "Well, okay, but I mean you have to go…

check." So Ella says, 'Well, I can't go on without you. I'm not going up there without drums, without a rhythm section.' You know. So she stayed back in the restaurant with me. So finally, Tim Gale comes back. He says, 'How about it, Kenny?' I said, 'I told you, Tim, I'm not going on until you give me my record check, because it has nothing to do with the drums. Now, please give me my check if you want us to play.' So he hemmed and hawed and hemmed and hawed and I said, 'Okay, you can hem and haw all you want,…
